newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes off its highs but well supported.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes off its highs but well supported.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed off its highs on Wednesday but was still well supported.
It ended at 5.00 p.m. (0400 GMT) at US$0.6910/17, down from the 0.6925 high, but well ahead of its 0.6895/05 close on Tuesday.
The Trade-Weighted Index ended in strong shape near nine year highs at 68.51 against its 68.37 opening.
Dealers said the lack of selling out of New York in the morning, a feature of the recent trading pattern, was a signal to take the kiwi higher.
Dealers said recent data on housing and private sector credit showed lingering inflationary pressures.
Valuation New Zealand said its quarterly index rose 2.5 percent in the December quarter, while private sector credit rose 2.1 percent in December.
Dealers expect the kiwi to remain in a 0.6875-0.6925 range over the Thursday bank holiday.

However, direction could be set by the U.S. on Thursday morning when a decision from the Federal Open Market Committee is expected. It is expected to hold rates and maintain support for a strong dollar.
